title: Self-Publishing In the Eye of the Storm
author: Orna Ross
target_audience: Independent writers seeking to understand the modern publishing landscape
Members of the Alliance of Independent Authors (ALLi)
Creative entrepreneurs navigating change and uncertainty
Industry observers interested in trends in publishing
core_themes: Adapting to industry upheaval and rapid technological change
The empowerment of authors through self-publishing
Sustaining creativity and resilience amid uncertainty
Community, advocacy, and the collective voice of indie authors
primary_purpose: To examine how independent authors can successfully navigate—and even thrive—amidst the volatility and transformation of the modern publishing industry, drawing on practical advice, industry trends, and author advocacy.

structure_format.organization: Combination of essays, firsthand accounts, industry analysis, and actionable advice
features: Personal narrative from the author’s experience as a writer and industry leader
Case studies and examples from the indie author community
Guidance on business models, marketing, and long-term sustainability

key_concepts_lessons: The publishing industry is in a state of continual change, driven by technology and shifting reader habits.
Self-publishing empowers authors but requires a dual focus on craft and business.
Building a supportive network/community is vital for indie author success.
Adaptability, resilience, and lifelong learning are crucial qualities for modern writers.
Advocacy and collective action help protect author rights and shape the future of publishing.
Understanding new trends—such as subscription models, direct sales, and AI tools—can unlock new opportunities.
notable_features: Insights from a leading figure in the indie publishing movement
Blends personal memoir with industry analysis and practical guidance
Addresses the impact of global events (e.g., the COVID-19 pandemic) on publishing
Focus on author advocacy and the collective power of the indie community
cultural_historical_context: Published post-pandemic during a period of accelerated change in publishing, marked by the rise of new technologies (e.g., AI, digital platforms), shifting business models, and heightened author advocacy. Reflects the growing recognition of self-publishing as a legitimate and often preferable route for many writers.
reception_impact: Praised in indie publishing circles for its honesty, encouragement, and actionable insights
Recognized as a valuable resource for both new and experienced self-publishers
Cited by industry organizations such as ALLi
Helps legitimize and demystify self-publishing for wider audiences
comparable_titles: The Business of Being a Writer by Jane Friedman
Let’s Get Digital by David Gaughran
How to Market a Book by Joanna Penn
The Indie Author Mindset by Adam Croft
